family_judgments.evidence: Cloze, dialogue completion, multiple choice, and cue-based production are all credible interface variants for practising the same everyday instructional exchange.
Every item repeats the same cake-and-oven scenario and exact response, so presenting the whole family to one learner would feel noticeably repetitive despite the format changes.

criteria.evidence: The instruction clearly states the two required expressions and the context establishes the next action.
A short-text response is suitable because the learner is asked to supply one complete instruction.
“cake,” “counter,” “oven,” and “turn off” are common, concrete vocabulary for B2 learners.
Removing a cake while leaving the oven on gives a credible reason for the instruction.
The brief controlled production task is appropriately accessible at B2.
The prompt, context, and single short-text field can be presented and scored straightforwardly in a simple practice interface.
The dialogue makes the speaker roles and required reply unambiguous.
Completing Alex’s labelled dialogue turn with short text matches the interaction requested.
The wording uses familiar household and cooking vocabulary.
Sam’s question, “What should I do next?”, naturally invites Alex’s instruction.
The contextual support and supplied wording make this an appropriate B2 production prompt.
A dialogue display plus one response field is conventional and needs no complex interface behaviour.
The instruction and stem both ask learners to identify the direct instruction Alex should use.
The four visible sentence options suit a single-choice interaction.
All options reuse simple, concrete vocabulary from the context.
The situation provides a believable need for an immediate instruction.
The alternatives are short and the distinction between an instruction and other sentence forms is suitable for B2 practice.
This is a standard single-select item with an unambiguous correct option.
The target action is clear, but “without adding a subject” is somewhat technical wording for an otherwise natural learner-facing instruction.
A full-sentence field is coherent for writing the requested direct instruction from the cue words.
The source sentence and cue words use familiar household vocabulary.
The source sentence gives enough realistic context for an instruction about the oven.
Turning the supplied cue words into a direct instruction is a plausible B2 controlled-production task.
The source sentence, cue words, and full-sentence input can be implemented in a simple interface and scored against the specified response.

summary: The family is clear, natural, and readily deployable; only the technical wording in the transformation instruction and repeated identical scenario create minor product-experience concerns.
